headline: Suki, whose AI tool writes up doctors' visit notes, has raised $90 million to build AI agents that handle follow-up tasks such as referrals and insurance approvals.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a confirmed funding round that points to AI scribes moving into paperwork beyond notes, but rivals raised more last year and the agents are not yet built.
importance_line: Doctors who use AI note-taking may later get tools that also file referrals and approvals, and Suki's technology partners will watch the plan, but the agents are planned rather than shipped and Suki raised less than rivals Ambience Healthcare ($243 million) and Abridge ($300 million) did last year.
summary: Healthcare Dive reports that Suki, whose AI scribe listens to doctor-patient visits and drafts clinical notes, has raised $90 million in a Series E funding round from new investors Healthier Capital, Crosslink Capital and Hercules Capital together with existing backers. Suki chief executive Punit Soni told Healthcare Dive the money will go to AI agents that complete tasks after a visit, such as referrals and prior authorizations (insurer approvals for treatments), and to deeper work with more than 30 technology partners, including Optum, Zoom and athenahealth, that build Suki's tools into their products.
notes: Original Fierce Healthcare page blocked (HTTP 403); Healthcare Dive text, based on its own interview with the chief executive, read in full. Business Wire, Axios (exclusive, evening of 12 Oct US time), Inc. and Modern Healthcare also carried it per Google News.
